pr_title: chrome_extensions: Refactor the table, add tests
pr_body:
This is a rewrite of the `chrome_extensions` and `chrome_extensions_content_scripts` virtual table implementations that makes them testable, adds tests, fixes problems with missed data in the results, and expands the schema. 

The schema additions for `chrome_extensions_content_scripts`: 
- include columns for `browser_type` (because it supports several Chrome-derived browsers)
- the Chrome profile path
- the path to the extension folder
- a boolean value for whether the extension is referenced from the profile's Preferences file. 

The schema additions for `chrome_extensions`: 
- `browser_type`
- `profile_path`
- the `locale` column is replaced by `default_locale` and `current_locale` 
- many columns sourced from the manifest.json
- a hash of the manifest file itself in order to monitor it for changes. 

These tables replace the `opera_extensions` tables, but in doing so, add support for querying Opera extensions on Windows.

~**Note** Build requirement on macOS is the 10.14 or higher SDK:
`cd build; cmake -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=10.14 -DOSQUERY_BUILD_TESTS=ON ..`~ Removed `std::optional` to avoid this requirement.

Fixes: #6069

issue_context.title: Testing Browser Tables Blueprint
issue_context.body:
In order to run unit tests on browser related tables (eg. chrome_extensions, firefox_addons) an instance of that browser must be present on the machine. 

Therefore an instance of the browser would have to be placed on the CI in order for testing to work properly. 

Is there an alternative way to support this?
comments:
That's a good question. 

I'm not sure how it would fit in this testing infra, but one way I've done this in the past is to ship the data files that it would be reading.

Using some static files pulled from a real Chrome profile seems like a good compromise, and would involve the least additional overhead on our CI builds.

We will just have to occasionally update these files in order to ensure that the tests are testing a semi-current version of Chrome profile file format.

review_comments: If you set `locale` as an alias of `default_locale` the data will be auto-copied if someone explicitly selects the `locale` column. Under the hood it becomes `HIDDEN`.
Should this be in the if block?
The intent here was to always initialize the column; in case the version field is not present in the properties, it will initialize the version column to an empty string

In the past we had some crashes due to code assuming that columns were present when in fact they were being left missing by the implementation; this gets harder when the implementation differs based on platform. Since then, I think we have all been trying to make sure that table code always populate all the columns listed in the schema

I remember issues based on whether or not a column is defined, platform specific columns end up being very hard to write generalized queries for. (There's a hack!)

But I don't remember crashes about null values. 

I feel like sqlite should support nulls cleanly. Else it's impossible to differentiate between an empty string and no data.

The crashes were caused by code inside osquery running queries against other tables, then trying to access columns that were not being populated by one or the other implementation.

sqlite does support NULL column values, but osquery was initially designed to always convert everything to string, causing that feature (and real types) to get lost.
